CONTEXT. The previous page parametrises five rational quantities α', β, γ', δ, ε'. With p:q = cos m : sin m and P:Q = cos M : sin M it gives α'^2 = tan m·tan M, β^2 = tan m/tan M, γ'^2 = tan2m/tan2M, δ^2 = tan(45°+m)·tan(45°−M) and ε'^2 = tan(45°−m)·tan(45°−M). It also gives a rule producing a new solution from an old one. The underlying geometric or Diophantine problem is not stated on these two pages. Its form is: find rational values such that several products of tangents are squares.

PART 1 (numerical solution). Here a symbol 'b/a' on the right-hand side means the angle arctan(b/a), '1' means arctan 1 = 45°, and '2.1' means 2·arctan 1 (this reading is mine, but every line checks). Each left-hand rational number is the tangent of the stated angle sum. Equivalently, it is the slope of a product of Gaussian integers: 2+i, 4+i, 8+3i, 3+2i, 6+5i and 1+i, with norms 5, 17, 73, 13, 61 and 2.
(α) 2·atan(1/2) + atan(1/4) + atan(3/8) − atan 1.
  - tan 2atan(1/2) = 4/3.
  - Adding atan(1/4) gives tan = 19/8.
  - Adding atan(3/8) gives tan = 176/7.
  - Subtracting 45° gives tan = (176−7)/(176+7) = 169/183. ✓
(β) −3·atan(1/2) + 90°.
  - tan 3atan(1/2) = 11/2, so the result is cot = 2/11. ✓
(γ) −atan(1/2) − atan(2/3) − atan(5/6) + 135°.
  - The three arctangents sum to an angle with tan = −62/11.
  - Then tan(135° − S) = (−1 + 62/11)/(1 + 62/11) = 51/73. ✓
(δ) atan(2/3) − atan(5/6) + 45°.
  - The difference has tan = −3/28.
  - Adding 45° gives (1 − 3/28)/(1 + 3/28) = 25/31. ✓
(ε) atan(3/8) − atan(1/4).
  - tan = (1/8)/(35/32) = 4/35. ✓
In Gaussian-integer terms the norms are:
  - 183²+169² = 2·5²·17·73
  - 11²+2² = 5³
  - 73²+51² = 2·5·13·61
  - 31²+25² = 2·13·61
  - 35²+4² = 17·73
The marginal note says this solution even belongs to the case where numerator and denominator are themselves squares ('nemlich 6,7 / 13,14'). It adds that it can be derived from the general rule (presumably the rule on the previous page) via '13,? → 12,1,14,27'. I cannot reconstruct this derivation with certainty.

PART 2 ('the most elegant form'). Let λ, λ' and an angle δ be given (Gauss overloads the letter δ: it is both an angle and the fifth quantity). He sets:
  - α' = tan(λ−λ')
  - β = tan(λ+λ'−δ)
  - γ'^2 = tan(2λ−δ)·tan(2λ'−δ)
  - δ^2 = sin(4λ'−2δ)/sin(4λ−2δ)
  - ε'^2 = tan(2λ'−δ)/tan(2λ−δ)
This has the same structure as the previous page, with m ↔ 2λ−δ and M ↔ 2λ'−δ, up to relabelling.
Rational substitution: tan λ = b/a, tan λ' = b'/a', tan δ = B/A. Define
  - 𝔄 = (a²−b²)A + 2abB
  - 𝔅 = 2abA − (a²−b²)B
  - 𝔄', 𝔅' similarly with a', b'.
The steps, with the implicit ones filled in by me:
  - tan 2λ = 2ab/(a²−b²), hence tan(2λ−δ) = 𝔅/𝔄.
  - 𝔄² + 𝔅² = (a²+b²)²(A²+B²), hence sin(4λ−2δ) = 2𝔄𝔅/((a²+b²)²(A²+B²)).
  - Therefore α' = (a'b−ab')/(aa'+bb').
  - β = [(a'b+ab')A − (aa'−bb')B]/[(aa'−bb')A + (a'b+ab')B].
  - γ' = √(𝔅𝔅'/(𝔄𝔄')).
  - δ = (a²+b²)/(a'²+b'²)·√(𝔄'𝔅'/(𝔄𝔅)).
  - ε' = √(𝔄𝔅'/(𝔅𝔄')).
All three radicands differ from 𝔄𝔅𝔄'𝔅' by square factors. So the single remaining condition is that 𝔄𝔅𝔄'𝔅' be a square, as Gauss states.
errors: No mathematical errors found: all five numerical tangent sums and all the Part 2 formulas check.
Notational clash: δ denotes both the fifth unknown and the auxiliary angle with tan δ = B/A. The clash is harmless but confusing.
Note 'δ = √(sin…/sin…)' is to be read as δ² equal to the ratio. The formula itself is consistent with the rational form given below it.
Title phrase '10fache Quadrate' and the marginal derivation '13,? → 12,1,14,27' cannot be verified from this page alone. The claim that the solution comes from (6,7), (13,14) is unchecked.

results.what: Representation of the rationals 169/183, 2/11, 51/73, 25/31, 4/35 as tangents of integer combinations of arctan(1/2), arctan(1/4), arctan(3/8), arctan(2/3), arctan(5/6) and arctan 1. This is equivalent to factoring a+bi into Gaussian primes.
results.usually_credited_to: Arctan addition: Machin/Euler (18th c.); Gaussian integers: Gauss 1832

results.what: Trigonometric parametrisation of the five unknowns by angles λ, λ', δ, followed by rational substitution tan = b/a. This reduces all square conditions to the single condition that 𝔄𝔅𝔄'𝔅' is a square.
results.modern_name: Rational (tangent half-angle) parametrisation reducing a system of square conditions to one quartic/elliptic-type condition
results.usually_credited_to: Diophantine method in the tradition of Diophantus and Euler

results.modern_name: Multiplicativity of sums of two squares (Brahmagupta–Fibonacci identity)

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a worked Diophantine computation using arctangent/Gaussian-integer arithmetic and a clean trigonometric reduction to one square condition. These techniques are entirely characteristic of Gauss and standard in the Euler tradition. The underlying problem is unidentified but appears to be a classical rational-figure problem; nothing here anticipates a later named result.

transcription_corrections: '2.1' and '3.1' mean 2·(1) and 3·(1), i.e. multiples of arctan 1 = 45°. Fractions such as '1/2' denote arctan(1/2).
Marginal '13,7 → 12,1,14,27': the second number before the arrow is unclear in the image ('13,;'), possibly '13,1'. The reading is uncertain.
'10fache Quadrate' in the title is a doubtful reading of the hand. The marginal note explicitly speaks of the case where numerator and denominator are 'selbst Quadrate'.
In the δ formula the second sine reads sin(4λ − 2δ) without a prime, matching the transcription. The radical sign in the β formula is a stray stroke; β is a plain fraction, not a square root.
